implementation_notes: kotlinx.coroutines supplies the mailbox: a Channel is a suspending queue (send and receive suspend instead of blocking), so the actor is a class with private state plus one launched consumer coroutine that loops over the channel and handles one message at a time - no synchronized, no locks. Choose the channel capacity deliberately, because the default Channel() has no buffer and send suspends until the actor receives, while Channel(capacity = n) is a real mailbox that backpressures senders at n. Closing the channel ends the loop and is the shutdown signal; cancellation propagates to child coroutines. What replaces the classic structure: one coroutine plus one Channel per actor.
pitfalls: The default Channel() is a rendezvous channel with no buffer, so send suspends until the actor receives; pick an explicit capacity when senders must not wait for a busy actor.
consumeEach cancels the channel when it completes, while a plain for-loop is the safe form when several coroutines fan out over one channel.
A blocking call inside the consumer coroutine blocks its dispatcher thread and every other coroutine on it; wrap it in withContext(Dispatchers.IO).
